exposure: Delayed newborn bath (until at least 12 hours of life)
outcome: Neonatal hypoglycemia (blood glucose level of 49 or less)
cohort: The study included data on 1135 newborns from an urban community hospital, with a pre-intervention sample of 578 births and a post-intervention sample of 557 births.
finding: Delaying the initial bath for newborns until at least 12 hours of life significantly decreased rates of hypoglycemia in both high-risk and low-risk infants.
